title: What an Operating System Does
hands_on: Create the portable OS lab workspace, inspect its container recipe, compile the starter C program, and record the compiler/runtime versions.
source_alignment: OSTEP Chapter 2 introduces the operating system’s core goals. This module connects those goals to mechanism-versus-policy reasoning and a reproducible C and Unix workflow.

title: Processes and Process APIs
reading_chapters: Chapter 4: The Abstraction: The Process | Chapter 5: Interlude: Process API
hands_on: Write a small C program that forks, prints parent/child PIDs, waits, and then add an exec call. Predict the output before running it.
source_alignment: OSTEP Chapters 4–5 explain the process abstraction and its APIs. This module turns that reading into fork, exec, wait, exit, and shell traces.

title: CPU Mechanisms and Scheduling
reading_chapters: Chapter 6: Mechanism: Limited Direct Execution | Chapter 7: Scheduling: Introduction | Chapter 8: Scheduling: The Multi-Level Feedback Queue | Chapter 9: Scheduling: Proportional Share | Chapter 10: Multiprocessor Scheduling
official_simulators: Chapter 7: FIFO/SJF scheduling metrics | Chapter 8: MLFQ priority and I/O behavior | Chapter 9: Lottery scheduling | Chapter 10: Multiprocessor scheduling and caches
hands_on: Run OSTEP scheduling simulators with at least three seeds. Draw one Gantt chart manually, then reconcile it with simulator output.
source_alignment: OSTEP Chapters 6–10 progress from limited direct execution to scheduling policies. This module emphasizes reproducible traces, response and turnaround metrics, and policy tradeoffs.

title: Address Spaces, Relocation, and Segmentation
reading_chapters: Chapter 13: The Abstraction: Address Spaces | Chapter 14: Interlude: Memory API | Chapter 15: Mechanism: Address Translation | Chapter 16: Segmentation
official_simulators: Chapter 15: Base-and-bounds relocation | Chapter 16: Two-segment translation
hands_on: Use the OSTEP relocation and segmentation simulators. For three addresses, compute the result by hand before revealing the simulator answer.
source_alignment: OSTEP Chapters 13–16 introduce address spaces, the memory API, relocation, and segmentation. This module focuses on protection checks, translation arithmetic, and fragmentation evidence.

title: Paging, TLBs, and Page Tables
reading_chapters: Chapter 18: Paging: Introduction | Chapter 19: Translation Lookaside Buffers | Chapter 20: Advanced Page Tables
official_simulators: Chapter 18: Linear page-table translation | Chapter 20: Multi-level page-table walk
hands_on: Use the OSTEP paging translation simulator, then write a tiny address-translation worksheet that labels VPN, offset, valid bit, and PFN.
source_alignment: OSTEP Chapters 18–20 develop paging, translation caches, and multi-level page tables. This module uses address decompositions and state tables to make each lookup step visible.

title: Demand Paging and Replacement
reading_chapters: Chapter 21: Swapping: Mechanisms | Chapter 22: Swapping: Policies
hands_on: Run page-replacement traces under FIFO, LRU, and Clock; explain one point where policies diverge.
source_alignment: OSTEP Chapters 21–22 explain demand paging and replacement policy. This module connects page-fault mechanisms to FIFO, LRU, OPT, and Clock traces under explicit frame counts.

title: Threads and Race Conditions
reading_chapters: Chapter 26: Concurrency: An Introduction | Chapter 27: Interlude: Thread API
hands_on: Compile a pthread counter program with and without `-fsanitize=thread`, reproduce a race, then protect the critical section.
source_alignment: OSTEP Chapters 26–27 introduce threads, shared state, and the pthread API. This module uses concrete interleavings to connect the abstraction to race and atomicity reasoning.

title: Locks and Correct Critical Sections
reading_chapters: Chapter 28: Locks | Chapter 29: Lock-based Concurrent Data Structures
hands_on: Implement a mutex-protected counter, then deliberately move one access outside the critical section and explain the broken invariant.
source_alignment: OSTEP Chapters 28–29 explain locks and lock-based data structures. This module connects critical-section invariants to mutex ownership, atomic primitives, and data-structure correctness.

title: Condition Variables and Semaphores
hands_on: Build a bounded-buffer or ordered-print exercise with pthread mutexes and condition variables; add a log that makes waiting and wakeup visible.
source_alignment: OSTEP Chapters 30–31 develop condition variables and semaphores. This module uses bounded-buffer and ordering cases to practice both safety and progress reasoning.

title: Deadlock and Liveness
hands_on: Create a two-lock deadlock under controlled conditions, capture thread stacks, then repair it with a documented lock order.
source_alignment: OSTEP Chapter 32 classifies common concurrency failures. This module connects wait-for graphs and the Coffman conditions to prevention, avoidance, detection, and non-deadlock bugs.

title: I/O Devices and Device Interaction
hands_on: Use `strace` in the container to observe open/read/write calls from a small C program; annotate which operations cross into the kernel.
source_alignment: OSTEP Chapter 36 explains the I/O path from software to devices. This module compares polling, interrupts, and DMA while tracing responsibility across the application, kernel, driver, and device.

title: Files, Directories, and Metadata
hands_on: Create a file, hard link, and symbolic link inside the lab workspace; compare `ls -li`, `stat`, and behavior after removing the original name.
source_alignment: OSTEP Chapter 39 explains files, directories, descriptors, links, and metadata. This module turns the APIs into state and namespace traces that distinguish names from open objects.

title: File-System Implementation and Crash Consistency
reading_chapters: Chapter 40: File System Implementation | Chapter 41: Fast File System | Chapter 42: Crash Consistency: FSCK and Journaling
official_simulators: Chapter 40: Very simple file-system state | Chapter 41: FFS placement policy | Chapter 42: File-system consistency diagnosis
hands_on: Walk a simplified VSFS image or diagram: resolve a pathname, identify inode/data bitmap changes for file creation, then mark crash points in an update sequence.
source_alignment: OSTEP Chapters 40–42 develop file-system layout, locality, and crash consistency. This module uses access-path and write-order traces to connect on-disk structures to recovery guarantees.
